status: An owner-ruled addition to the surface contract, recorded beside the Product Designer's authored artifact rather than edited into it. C-20 requires the isolation procedure to run on "every journey" and nothing said what the journeys were, so the word had no referent and the claim could not be checked.
why: A journey is a sequence, not a state. Running isolation over twenty end-states would miss a leak that only happens in transit, which is exactly where a save, a retry or a refusal does its work.
notCoveredHere: Reload. The capture surface is deliberately non-persistent across page loads, so a browser reload cannot restore state there. Reload restoration is verified at the component level, where the adapter is injected and can be inspected after the fact.

steps.open-defer: activate the Defer control and wait for the editor
steps.type-overlong-reason: enter a reason past its bound
steps.set-future-date: enter a review date after the injected clock
steps.set-past-date: enter a review date before the injected clock
steps.inspect-evidence: activate the Inspect control on a resolved evidence link
steps.attempt-disabled-action: attempt to activate an action control that is disabled

journeys.why: the shortest complete path that writes twice and reverses itself
the long path, and the only one that carries free text into the record
a refusal is a journey; it renders, announces and moves focus like any other outcome
the refusal that could not be reached at all until decision 7-A
the only refusal raised by the core rather than by the form
the adapter rejects, input is preserved, and focus moves to retry
the one interaction that reads an artifact, and so the one most able to leave the fixture
a state reached by the clock alone, with nothing written
activation must change nothing, and the controls are present rather than removed
